findings.description: Priority 1 recommendation – generic advice to give every custom control an accessible name and correct role without any selector, page URL or instance count.
Priority 2 recommendation – generic instruction to raise contrast ratios for flagged text without referencing specific elements or pages.
Priority 3 recommendation – generic guidance to make every id attribute unique within each page, lacking a selector or data anchor.
Priority 4 recommendation – generic call to add descriptive alt text to images without specifying which images or pages.
Priority 5 recommendation – generic advice to expose table structure via ids, not tied to specific th elements or tables.
Priority 6 recommendation – generic instruction to add a skip link as the first focusable element, without naming the target page or selector.
Priority 7 recommendation – generic guidance to order headings without skipping levels, lacking specific heading instances.
Priority 8 recommendation – generic advice to replace landmark containers with semantic elements and give remaining containers meaningful class names, no selector or page reference.
Priority 9 recommendation – generic instruction to profile the slow route and cache or precompute expensive paths, without specifying URLs or selectors.
Priority 10 recommendation – generic call to add missing response headers at the server or CDN edge, not tied to specific endpoints.
Priority 11 recommendation – generic instruction to complete SEO metadata (title, meta description, canonical) without naming affected pages.
Priority 12 recommendation – generic advice to add missing Schema.org properties to flagged entity types, lacking specific entities or selectors.
Priority 13 recommendation – identical generic guidance as Priority 12, still without data anchors.
Priority 14 recommendation – generic instruction to publish llms.txt at the site root, not referencing a specific file path or selector.
